Release note drafted and the mechanism is in place.

PR #950 is labelled 'type: breaking', so the change lands under Breaking in the drafted release. Release Drafter only emits PR titles, so the consumer-facing paragraph was posted as a comment on #950 for whoever cuts the release to paste into the draft: morphir-runtime_3 stops being produced, consumers move to morphir-runtime-classic_3, the Scala package is unchanged so it is a build-file change only, and morphir-naming_3 / morphir-model_3 appear as new artifacts with morphir depending transitively on naming.

Flagged on the PR as well: 'type: breaking' maps to a major bump in version-resolver, which on a 0.x line resolves to 1.0.0 and is very likely not intended. The tag should be set deliberately at release time.

The detail also remains in morphir/model/CONTRIBUTING.md item 7, which is the checked-in copy.

The 'consider configuring MiMa' half of this issue is split into morphir-1pr rather than dropped — and note MiMa would not actually have caught this, since it compares an artifact against its own previous version and says nothing when one disappears.

Resolved in fc575135 by dropping the trait rather than by publishing the modules.

All seven trees — langkit/core, langkit/trees, langkit/elm/core, langkit/elm/compiler/api, kit/kyo, intelligence, intelligence/sdk — no longer extend MorphirPublishModule / MorphirIntelligencePublishModule. Publishing them would have committed those coordinates and their API surface permanently, since a Maven Central release cannot be withdrawn, and none is ready for that. Nothing in the published set depends on them, so nothing downstream changes.

./mill resolve 'morphir.__.publishSonatypeCentral' now yields exactly the modules the publish command names plus the mill-morphir-elm plugin it deliberately excludes, so the discrepancy is gone by construction. The publish task records that invariant, the resolve command to check it, and the rule that a module which should not ship drops the trait instead of being omitted from the list.

Answers to the two questions this issue posed: intelligence and intelligence/sdk used MorphirIntelligencePublishModule, which is just MorphirPublishModule with a different pom organization, so no separate publish path existed for them. And the drift concern is addressed by making the trait the single declaration of intent, rather than by a CI guard.

Two reversible costs, recorded in the commit message: these modules lose publishLocal, and they fall out of the  smoke test in test:jvm/test:js. Re-adding the trait restores both when any of them is ready to be released.

Verified with lint, test:jvm, test:js and test:native, all green.
